implemented_requirements.evidence: config.py defines BEGINNER, INTERMEDIATE, EXPERT as Difficulty namedtuples and DIFFICULTY_LEVELS list; gui._build_menu iterates over DIFFICULTY_LEVELS to create menu entries.
gui.__init__ binds left‑click events to a method _on_left_click, but the method is not defined in the provided files, so the uncover action cannot be performed.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate adjacent mines
implemented_requirements.evidence: board._compute_adjacent_counts correctly calculates adjacent_mines for each Cell, but there is no GUI code that reads this value and displays it on the button after a reveal.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Loss when a mine is uncovered
implemented_requirements.evidence: board.reveal checks cell.is_mine and calls self._lose(cell); _lose sets status to STATUS_LOST and records the explosion site.
gui.__init__ calls self._update_display(), but no _update_display method is defined, so the visual board never refreshes.
board.toggle_flag toggles Cell.is_flagged; gui binds right‑click events to _on_right_click (method not shown) which would invoke board.toggle_flag.
config defines FLAG_SYMBOL and FLAG_BG color, but the GUI never sets button text or background based on a cell's flagged state.

critical_issues: Missing implementation of _update_display() causes AttributeError during GUI initialization.
Methods _on_left_click and _on_right_click (which would call board.reveal and board.toggle_flag) are not defined, so user interaction cannot trigger game logic.
No code updates button text/background to show numbers, mines, or flag symbols, breaking the visual feedback requirement.
Without display updates, the game cannot show win/lose status or the remaining mine counter.
judge.summary: The repository contains solid core game logic (board, cell, difficulty configuration) and a Tkinter GUI skeleton, but the GUI is incomplete: essential methods for handling clicks and refreshing the display are missing, and flagged cells lack a distinct visual representation. Consequently the application would not run correctly, and several core user‑facing requirements are unfulfilled.
